04 · RELATIONSHIPS

Temperature and rainfall show little linear association

−0.02Lag-0 temperature–precipitation correlation

Correlation does not establish causation. Lagged relationships can be explored separately.

05 · TIME-SERIES STRUCTURE

Decomposition and lag dependence

The decomposition uses a 7-day period as an exploratory diagnostic. One year of data is not enough to estimate a robust annual seasonal component.
06 · STATIONARITY

First differencing improves stationarity evidence

TestOriginal seriesAfter first difference
ADF p-value0.7621.43 × 10⁻¹⁴
KPSS p-value0.0100.0503
Original series

ADF does not reject the unit-root null; KPSS rejects stationarity. The results support treating the original series as non-stationary.

Differenced series

ADF strongly rejects the unit-root null. KPSS is borderline, so stationarity is improved but should not be treated as conclusively proven by one test.

07 · DATA QUALITY & LIMITATIONS

Transparent checks, careful interpretation

Quality checks

  • Missing dates and values
  • Duplicate timestamps
  • NASA POWER fill value −999
  • Suspicious temperature and precipitation values
  • Global IQR and 30-day rolling z-score outliers

Limitations

  • NASA POWER is gridded/reanalysis-based, not a direct local station measurement.
  • Precipitation estimates can be uncertain in dry regions.
  • Only one year is available, limiting annual-seasonality conclusions.
  • Outlier flags are reviewed, not automatically deleted.
Takeaway: Banha’s 2025 weather data show a strong seasonal temperature contrast, sparse rainfall, and a temperature series that benefits from differencing before time-series modeling.
